title: Log Guardian: Terraform module for CloudTrail delivery, OpenSearch lifecycle, and automated health checks
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a reusable Terraform module (log-guardian) that standardizes CloudTrail S3 delivery, KMS-protected cross-account archives, OpenSearch ingest pipelines, and index lifecycle management (ILM)/retention policies for Redwood Private deployments. The module must include automated health checks, smoke tests for ingest and query, and upgrade paths for older on-prem Terraform stacks. Goal: one module customers can drop into their VPC blueprint and run with sane defaults while exposing knobs for enterprise retention, encryption, and cross-account ownership.
acceptance_criteria: Module provisions CloudTrail bucket, S3 notifications, and a connector that writes to OpenSearch ingest stream in private VPCs
KMS keys are created with proper grants for cross-account archive (customer-managed key optional)
Index lifecycle policies created with 30/90/365 day tiers configurable via variables
Module exposes boolean to enable/disable CloudTrail S3-to-OpenSearch ingestion for customers who manage their own log pipeline
Automated health checks: (1) CloudTrail delivery latency < 2 minutes for new events, (2) OpenSearch ingest pipeline success rate > 99% for 24h window
Migration path documented for Terraform state changes and provider upgrades (aws provider v3 -> v4 example)
Module includes terraform-level smoke test (apply in a sandbox account) and an automated CI job that validates core resources
Documentation + example usage included in repo and linked from Private deployment quickstart
tasks: Design variable surface and defaults (retention_days, enable_archive, kms_key_id, cross_account_grant, enable_healthchecks)
Implement CloudTrail S3 sink, ensure bucket encryption and lifecycle rules map to customer retention variables
Add SNS+Lambda or S3 event-based connector for pushing events to OpenSearch ingest (option for Kinesis Firehose)
Create OpenSearch ingest template, pipeline, and ILM policies with parametric rollover thresholds
Implement healthcheck Lambda that verifies recent delivery timestamps and OpenSearch write metrics; publish to CloudWatch and Redwood Console via metrics exporter
Write migration guide and sample tfstate shim for existing stacks using legacy logging modules
Add unit/acceptance tests and CI job in infra-ci to run smoke apply/destroy in a sandbox account
Security review + automated scanning (tfsec, checkov) and optional hardening presets for FIPS/KMS/HSM customers
notes: Tradeoff: Firehose simplifies ingestion and buffering but adds cost; lambda connector gives more control and easier on-prem fallback.
Prefer server-side KMS encryption for buckets by default; expose toggle for customer-managed keys if they need cross-account archival ownership.
Avoid putting large binary archives into OpenSearch; maintain separate archival S3 lifecycle for raw CloudTrail files and indexes only for query-relevant events.
Compatibility: must support existing private deployments using aws provider v3 and v4; use explicit provider version pinning and a migration shim where necessary.

rollback_plan: If a deployment causes missed delivery or index corruption, disable ingestion variable (enable_ingest=false) and revert to raw S3-only archival. Restore previous tfstate and run a reindex job from preserved raw events. Escalate to on-call infra leads and open an incident channel.
test_plan: Create sandbox apply that provisions module with default vars and with hardened vars; run smoke test to assert CloudTrail files appear in S3 within 60s
Run ingest test suite that sends synthetic CloudTrail events and verifies OpenSearch documents within 2 minutes
Run ILM policy test by creating indices with synthetic sizes and validate rollover and delete actions via ES APIs
CI job to run tf plan and tflint/tfsec on each PR
migration_instructions: For customers on legacy-logging-v1 module: export tfstate for logging resources, map bucket and key ARNs to new module inputs, run terraform import for new resources using mapping script located in migrations/legacy-to-guardian.sh

Provider upgrade note: when migrating aws provider v3 -> v4, run 'terraform state replace-provider' following the example in migrations/provider-upgrade.md and validate resource addresses in sandbox before production rollout
If using customer-managed KMS, pass kms_key_id and set enable_cross_account_grant=false; otherwise module will create and grant a new key
